title: Doesn't cool as well as window units with lower BTUs
text:
Doesn't cool as well as window units with lower BTUs. If you are looking at the 12,000 or even 14,000 BTU ac units to cool larger spaces, be aware that these portable machines aren't quite as capable as traditional window units of the same BTU measurements. I don't really understand why that's the case, but it is. We have a 640sqft weekend cabin with two window units in it - one is 8,000 BTU and the other is 10,000. They keep the cabin a very comfortable 72 degrees all summer - even when it's 96 degrees outside with a heat index of 104. So that's my base point for comparing this portable, 12,000 BTU machine to our existing set up.

This machine loses out to window units in a small space because it takes up floor space and still needs to occupy window space for the vent hose. Yes, it can be relocated to a different room if needed, but you still have to have a free window there and a three prong outlet - this is on wheels, but it weighs the same as a window unit.

As to the actual cooling ability....well that depends on your room size and insulation and the weather. I'm in East Texas with both high heat and high humidity so our heat index (misery factor) has been 102 to 105 for the past week. I first used this machine in the cabin living area - about 350sqft and the upper limit of this unit's ability. I normally have the 10,000 BTU window in that area. This machine does cool, but nowhere as effectively as the window unit - it never felt quite as comfortable as normal and we ended up going back to the window unit on the second day.

We moved this to the bedroom next - roughly 275sqft and cooled very effectively by an 8,000 BTU window air conditioner. The Midea portable did cool just as well and the room stayed at 72 degrees for three days of use. However, it required removing a small chair to accommodate this air conditioner and that's a big negative for me. Every inch counts in a small space.

For us, the window units are definitely more comfortable/cooler in the cabin and they certainly take less space and trouble. Yeah, window ACs are ugly and a portable can't be seen outside, but that is less important than being cool to us. I don't care what it looks like if it's 98 degrees outside and 72 in the cabin. In the end, this machine will be relegated to an emergency back up only.
